narrative: PL3__M0B0F8EE is a high-volume material averaging 3,229 units/day over 228 working days with no statistically significant trend (p=0.064). Lead times are unstable (CV=0.79), driven by transport variability, creating substantial lead-time demand uncertainty (sigma_LTD=3,506). The (s,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-based order quantity (12,858) and a z=1.6449 safety stock (5,768) achieves 95% service level within the 18,719-unit storage cap while reducing total annual cost by 88% versus the current MOQ-only SAP policy.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0 — no buffer against lead-time or demand variability; 5,768 units recommended.
Storage capacity near-binding: SS+OQ=18,626 vs cap=18,719 (~94 units headroom); monitor for safety stock revisions.
Lead time CV=0.79 classified as unstable; transport disruptions are dominant risk (60% of variance).
9 zero-demand days detected (likely plant shutdowns); these inflate classical std vs. robust std significantly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: High-volume, near-continuous demand (96% non-zero days) with unstable lead times makes a continuous-review (s,Q) policy optimal: it monitors inventory continuously and triggers a fixed EOQ replenishment when stock hits the reorder point, providing tight control over service level in the face of lead-time volatility.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 18,719 is nearly fully consumed (SS+OQ=18,626). Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g. if service level target rises or lead-time volatility worsens) would require a compensating reduction in order quantity below EOQ, increasing ordering frequency and cost.
